text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pluralist National Assembly (lower house) resumes session to decide whether to elect a speaker first or vote on the assembly's internal regulations.
- Polisario and Morocco confirm their participation in direct talks in Portugal on the Western Sahara.
- Bargaining on government line-up still raging: opposition groups refuse to join a coalition government while others were bidding higher to try to gain more cabinet portfolios.

- Abdelkader Bensalah is most likely to be elected lower house speaker. Bensalah is the head of the National Democratic Rally (RND) which groups President Liamine Zeroual's supporters. The RND is the biggest party in the house with 155 seats but it needs the backing of other groups to get an absolute majority in the 380-seat house.

- Local elections expected in October. Elected local authorities will select two-thirds of Algeria's Council of the Nation (upper house). The head of state names the other third of the 144-member upper house. The house and the National Assembly, elected early in June, form the Algerian parliament.

- Mahfoud Nahnah, leader of the Islamist-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS), says his party still the first political force in Algeria. The MPS came second in the number of seats won, taking 69 against the 155 of the RND group, in the June 5 legislative elections.
